incidents-bot: Pager triggered — GPU pool 'eu-west-3' capacity_high_queue_alert. queue_length=12432, enqueue_rate=780/s, evictions=317/min, xid_errors=high
SRE-Oncall: i'm paged and looking. seeing a steady queue ramp since ~02:12 UTC. dashboard shows autoscaler attempts but scale kept failing.
maria: which pool + what models are hot? any obvious customer traffic spike?
SRE-Oncall: pool=redwood-eu-west3-gpu-pool-7. top consumers right now: model-gpt-small-prod (~41%), rerank-batch (~22%), embed-stream (~10%). some tails from internal workloads. node flaps reported on node-7 and node-9; node-9 shows repeated CUDA/Xid and OOM entries.
prateek: past 10m from autoscaler logs:
prateek: ```
[2024-03-18T02:19:58Z] autoscaler: evaluate scale up -> need +8 gpus
[2024-03-18T02:20:05Z] autoscaler: quota check failed: available=0, requested=8
[2024-03-18T02:20:12Z] autoscaler: backoff(30s) due to rate-limit
[2024-03-18T02:20:45Z] autoscaler: attempt to attach nodes -> driver-manager timeout
```
infra-bot: pulling driver logs from node-9 and node-7. grep shows multiple Xid entries and kernel oopses on node-9. sample: `NVRM: Xid (31) at 0x...` and `oom_killer invoked for process nvidia-driver`.
eng-runtime: confirmed. driver process crashed 3x in last 12 minutes on node-9, causing GPUs to deregister briefly. effective_capacity dropped by ~18%.
SRE-Oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon+drain node-9, 2) enable fallback routing to reserved-dedicated pool eu-west3-ded-1, 3) reduce non-critical batch jobs, 4) open support banner if customer impact > threshold. executing now.
prateek: running cordon/drain
prateek: ```bash
kubectl cordon node-9
kubectl drain node-9 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 -l role!=critical
```
maria: i'll push a soft-traffic-shift to reserved pool and lower concurrency for model-gpt-small-prod to 2 per-worker to reduce pressure.
infra-bot: route change executed: `rwctl route update --from pool=redwood-eu-west3-gpu-pool-7 --to pool=eu-west3-ded-1 --mode=gradual --pct=40`
SRE-Oncall: monitor metrics. queue length dropping slowly but evictions still elevated. autoscaler still reporting quota=0; opsfinance says no immediate quota to spin up extra GPUs. looks like we hit a capacity cap for the region.
support-lead: CS watch: 24 customer complaints in last 30m referencing timeouts/503s. error-rate=5.8% (30m window). p95 latency from 1.1s -> 3.2s. some enterprise tenants on dedicated plans unaffected.
eng-runtime: driver team suggests forcing newer driver kernel on node-9 nodeset, but that's a rolling disruptive op. short-term we should keep problematic nodes drained and rely on dedicated pools and throttles. also recommend bumping model-level retry backoff to limit amplified enqueue on failure.
SRE-Oncall: implemented model throttles and reduced batch window for rerank-batch. trying to avoid cascade of retries.
prateek: autoscaler backoff cleared once quota was manually bumped by capacity-ops (requested emergency burst +6 GPUs to eu-west3 pool), but nodes are slow to register due to driver instability. logs: `node-register timeout, driver not responding`
infra-bot: new nodes attached: node-21..node-26 started registering, node-24 shows Xid warnings but still registered. net capacity now +12 GPUs but effective usable +6 (driver errors removed 6).
maria: customer impact update: we opened incident banner and notified top 10 customers (CS + account-led). reduced throttles helped lower 503 rate by ~40% over 10m. queue now 7.3k and trending down.
SRE-Oncall: next actions: continue draining any nodes with repeated Xid/oom, coordinate with driver on-call to push kernel driver hotfix, keep autoscaler monitor, and prepare pager handover in 20m.
support-lead: logging customer tickets to incident doc and tagging priority accounts for AM follow-up.
eng-runtime: i've captured a driver stack trace and uploaded to internal artifact store: link=https://artifacts.redwood.internal/driver-traces/4187654321-node9-xid31.txt
SRE-Oncall: summary for handoff -> Root cause hypothesis: driver/runtime instability (OOM + CUDA/Xid) reduced effective capacity while autoscaler was rate/quotaconstrained; that combination drove queue growth and customer-facing errors. Mitigations applied: drained node-9, soft-failed rerank batch, reduced concurrency for hot models, partial failover to reserved-dedicated pool, emergency quota bump, and ongoing driver investigation. Current status: queue trending down (7.3k), error-rate falling (now 3.4%), some customers still affected but degraded.
SRE-Oncall: handing over to maria (next oncall). maria — please continue watch, coordinate driver hotfix with eng-runtime, confirm full node stabilization, and start incident writeup. include cost/quota follow-up w/ capacity-ops.
maria: taking over. will keep 15m cadence updates and escalate to eng-runtime for a hotfix rollout plan. tagging @prateek for autoscaler logs for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
